classification.difficultyReason: Calculate missing interior angles, including from exterior angles, and test for two equal angles.

content.prompt: Determine whether each triangle $\triangle ABC$ below is an isosceles triangle. Give reasons.

spec.description: Triangle ABC with A above horizontal BC and both base angles labelled 63 degrees. Ordinary source blue strokes become black.

answer.worked: $\angle B=\angle C=63^\circ$, so the opposite sides $AC$ and $AB$ are equal. Therefore $\triangle ABC$ is isosceles.

spec.description: Triangle ABC with A above horizontal BC, angle A labelled 55 degrees and angle B labelled 62.5 degrees.
spec.mathematics: Angle A = 55 degrees; angle B = 62.5 degrees.

answer.worked:
Using the angle sum of $\triangle ABC$:
$$\begin{align*}\angle C&=180^\circ-55^\circ-62.5^\circ\\\angle C&=62.5^\circ\end{align*}$$
$\angle B=\angle C$, so $AC=AB$ and the triangle is isosceles.

spec.description: Right triangle with horizontal BC, vertical CA, right-angle square at C and 40-degree angle at B.
spec.mathematics: Angle B = 40 degrees; angle C = 90 degrees.

answer.worked:
Using the angle sum of $\triangle ABC$:
$$\begin{align*}\angle A&=180^\circ-90^\circ-40^\circ\\\angle A&=50^\circ\end{align*}$$
All three angles are different, so the triangle is not isosceles.

spec.description: B at left, A above C at right; BA extends beyond A. The 159-degree label lies outside the triangle beside AC; 74 degrees is inside at B.
spec.mathematics: Interior angle B = 74 degrees; exterior angle at A = 159 degrees.

answer.short: No; the interior angles are $21^\circ$, $74^\circ$ and $85^\circ$.
answer.worked:
Using the straight angle at $A$:
$$\begin{align*}\angle BAC&=180^\circ-159^\circ\\\angle BAC&=21^\circ\end{align*}$$
Using the angle sum of $\triangle ABC$:
$$\begin{align*}\angle ACB&=180^\circ-21^\circ-74^\circ\\\angle ACB&=85^\circ\end{align*}$$
All three angles are different, so the triangle is not isosceles.

spec.description: A lies upper left, C on a horizontal line and B to its right. BC extends left of C; its exterior angle with CA is labelled 54 degrees. Angle B is 27 degrees.
spec.mathematics: Exterior angle at C = 54 degrees; interior angle B = 27 degrees.
spec.answerVisibility: No calculated angles or equality marks appear.

answer.worked:
The exterior angle at $C$ equals the sum of the opposite interior angles:
$$\begin{align*}\angle A+27^\circ&=54^\circ\\\angle A&=54^\circ-27^\circ\\\angle A&=27^\circ\end{align*}$$
$\angle A=\angle B$, so $BC=AC$ and the triangle is isosceles.

spec.description: Triangle ABC with A above horizontal BC, BC extended right beyond C, interior angle B labelled 42.5 degrees and exterior angle C labelled 105 degrees.
spec.mathematics: Angle B = 42.5 degrees; exterior angle at C = 105 degrees.

answer.short: No; the interior angles are $62.5^\circ$, $42.5^\circ$ and $75^\circ$.
answer.worked:
Using the straight angle at $C$:
$$\begin{align*}\angle ACB&=180^\circ-105^\circ\\\angle ACB&=75^\circ\end{align*}$$
Using the angle sum of $\triangle ABC$:
$$\begin{align*}\angle BAC&=180^\circ-75^\circ-42.5^\circ\\\angle BAC&=62.5^\circ\end{align*}$$
All three angles are different, so the triangle is not isosceles.
